scope: Structural review of all 1069 exported plaintext HTTP bodies, including copies moved to duplicates/. No flag search, hidden-data decoding, external requests or script execution.

findings.observation: Whitespace character Wikipedia page appears 10 times.
findings.interpretation: Possible hint for the already solved ODT whitespace encoding; not proof of another flag.

findings.observation: testing/secrets.html is identical to the FIRST homepage body, which occurs 14 times.
findings.interpretation: Interesting URL name does not indicate unique body content.

findings.observation: Many unrelated local paths serve byte-identical copies of CERT-SE, FRA, NCSC, ENISA, Wikipedia and Riksdag pages.
Comments largely contain navigation templates, CMS component labels or Wikipedia parser diagnostics. Hidden elements largely correspond to menus, cookie widgets, reader controls or collapsed UI.
findings.interpretation: No specific hidden-content lead established by this structural review; not an exhaustive content clearance.

findings.observation: The two Riksdag bodies contain large __NEXT_DATA__ JSON script blocks.
findings.interpretation: Recognizable Next.js page state; not decoded or executed.

findings.observation: 1072 GET requests and one POST, to the OCSP responder. Sixteen local URLs use query paths of the form /?/name.html.
findings.interpretation: No non-OCSP upload request in the extracted request inventory.

limitations: No comparison against live public originals.
No claim that HTML, scripts, headers, cookies or timing are free of hidden data.
ODT and PNG were both HTTP transfers and already produced flags; no additional HTML-body flag established.
